cause: No number at all: the core's stack-growth crate has no Android backend, so every pass runs on a heap segment and the first facade upcall from it throws StackOverflowError. The device runner stays non-gating until it is fixed.
≈7 µs per bound item (the 100k list's 62 ms first paint is the same cost): every item's key, extents and data clone are materialised, even outside the window, and a rebind walks everything twice.
10,000 nodes read back as per-node JSON, 10,000 TextKit measurements with no (text, style) memo, visuals read for every index; the rebind pays the removed and the fresh nodes.

100,000 rows serialised to a JSON string in Swift and parsed again in Rust; then 275 facade calls, 34 KB and 78 text measures per scroll step (nodesAt for removed and added rows, a visual and a text style per node).
Four cells per row re-read and re-measured per step, typed cells resolved through recipe parts on every read-back; a sort (47 ms) rebuilds every row instead of re-ordering.
The JVM facade's first touch: JNA load, UniFFI contract checks and per-function lazy lookups, the ICU formatter and the font resolver warm-up (a second model paints in 29 ms).
The whole nodes() list is re-read as JSON on every re-window instead of the facade's delta; 182 calls per step, 12 MB over a 200-message stream; a step is 2× the core.
Per-node JSON parsing in readNodes, a Compose text measure per item with no memo, visuals read for every index.
Four cells per row re-read and re-measured per step, recipe parts resolved per cell; 2× the List's step.
Every updateComponents reduces the whole surface again and every node object is new, so every transcript card re-renders; the late messages (p95 36 ms) miss a 60 Hz frame.

A mode flip runs the full theme path (the stylesheet recompiled, every node re-rendered, Chromium's style recalc under a new scope class) although only the mode variables differ; a theme switch is 70 ms.
The container-query context changes so every node re-renders and the responsive section remounts; the 48-deep chain's 73 ms first paint for 95 nodes points at per-level work too.
10,000 DOM nodes in one commit; a rebind where every key changes reuses nothing and removes the old nodes one by one.
The jump renders the window at the estimated offset, reads the extents back and re-aims, so the window renders twice with 30 fresh rows each time; ten scroll steps' worth.
